response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT ordersmark, COUNT(*) AS exec_count FROM orderexecutions GROUP BY ordersmark), s AS (SELECT ordersmark, exec_count, 1.0*exec_count/SUM(exec_count) OVER () AS share FROM g) SELECT ordersmark AS order_reference, exec_count, share, share - AVG(share) OVER () AS share_minus_avg FROM s ORDER BY share_minus_avg DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Executions with a NULL ordersmark form one group, which GROUP BY produces automatically and which counts as one order reference in the average share. The total is the count of all execution rows, including NULL-reference rows.
The average share is the unweighted mean of per-group shares, so it equals 1 divided by the number of groups.
